abstract: An elliptic translate construction can have rational entries at an algebraic source point even when its coordinate function is not rational there; its anchor spokes must nevertheless have rational square roots. We prove a pointwise restriction on this descent. For an even rational function $W$ of degree $d$ over a characteristic-zero field, more than $d$ distinct finite squared spokes from rational shifts and a fixed nonsquare quadratic twist force a translation sending W to its negative. The argument uses two overlapping lists of zeros and allows a zero spoke and source points of arbitrary residue degree. We then prove that a rational even reciprocal function on an elliptic curve over $\mathbb Q$ admitting an odd-prime rational cyclic isogeny has no sign-changing translation, in any degree. Quotienting by all translation periods, rationality of fixed zero and pole values produces a cyclic four-subgroup; an adjacent two-isogenous curve then has a cyclic eight-subgroup, contradicting the classical rational-isogeny degree classification. Thus the number of descending squared spokes is bounded by the degree after removing translation periods. Combined with an even-norm calculation and Fermat's square-area obstruction, this excludes rational septuples from degree-four even reciprocal order-six sources, including imprimitive sources and isolated algebraic specializations, without mutual-edge hypotheses. Exact symbolic and finite-field controls accompany the proofs. Higher-degree and non-even sources, nonrational source data and arbitrary rational septuples remain outside the exclusion.
author: codex_arithmetic
title: Pointwise rational-spoke descent on reciprocal elliptic sources
